canonical_statement: The meta-analysis evaluated dapagliflozin versus placebo as add-on therapy to conventional antidiabetic drugs for glycaemic control and body-weight effects in adults with type 2 diabetes.
Only randomized controlled trials were eligible; observational, cohort, case-control, case-series, and laboratory studies were excluded.

population.label: Eligibility criteria
exclusion_criteria: Observational, cohort, case-control, case-series, laboratory studies

canonical_statement: For HbA1c analyses, eligible randomized trials required follow-up longer than 8 weeks.

population.label: Eligibility criteria
inclusion_criteria: Follow-up longer than 8 weeks for HbA1c

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Eligible interventions combined dapagliflozin with conventional antidiabetic drugs; dapagliflozin monotherapy was excluded.
Eligible comparators used placebo combined with the corresponding conventional antidiabetic drug; placebo-only control groups were excluded.
Eligible trials had to measure all three outcomes: HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, and body weight.

inclusion_criteria: HbA1c, FPG, and body weight all measured

Across outcome analyses, included trials enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes and had follow-up durations from 12 to 104 weeks.

The review followed PRISMA, and its protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO as CRD42013005034.
Literature searches covered PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov; the initial search was 9 July 2013 and the last update was 21 October 2013.
The search used dapagliflozin and diabetes terms, supplemented by Google searching and manual journal searching for randomized-trial information not captured by database indexing.
At least two reviewers evaluated study eligibility; extracted data were taken by one reviewer and verified by another, with disagreements resolved by discussion.
Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane tool and outcome-level evidence quality with GRADE profiler 3.2.
Meta-analysis used R 3.0.1 with the metafor package and Review Manager 5.2, with p<0.05 treated as statistically significant.
A random-effects model compared changes in HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, and body weight between the 10 mg dapagliflozin arm and placebo arm.
Continuous outcomes were extracted as adjusted mean differences with 95% confidence intervals, and pooled effects were calculated as mean differences of those adjusted mean differences.
Prespecified subgroup analyses stratified results by combined antidiabetic drug and by follow-up duration of 24 weeks or less versus more than 24 weeks.
Meta-regression assessed the association between follow-up duration and each pooled outcome.
Publication bias was assessed with funnel plots and Egger regression and adjusted with trim-and-fill; heterogeneity was summarized with I-squared.
Sensitivity analyses excluded trials with more than one unclear risk-of-bias item and separately excluded interim reports so only endpoint results remained.
The search assessed 380 citations: 231 from bibliographic databases and 149 from supplementary Google and Google Scholar searching; 12 RCTs remained for quantitative synthesis.
The included studies covered five add-on drug settings: metformin, insulin, glimepiride, pioglitazone, and metformin/sitagliptin.
Included trials used dapagliflozin doses of 2.5, 5, and 10 mg, while the principal pooled comparison used 10 mg.
Four included RCTs were interim reports and eight RCTs with final results were retained for the endpoint-only sensitivity analysis.
Most included RCTs used last-observation-carried-forward handling, with extracted adjusted mean differences derived from ANCOVA models.
Four RCTs had more than one risk-of-bias item rated unclear, with lack of reported blinding as the common detection-bias concern.
GRADE rated the HbA1c evidence as high quality.
GRADE rated the fasting-plasma-glucose evidence as high quality.
GRADE rated the body-weight evidence as moderate quality because of publication bias.
The HbA1c funnel plot and Egger test did not indicate statistically significant publication bias.
The fasting-plasma-glucose funnel plot and Egger test did not indicate statistically significant publication bias.
The body-weight funnel plot and Egger test indicated publication bias.
Excluding trials with more than one unclear risk-of-bias item produced results that the authors judged similar to the primary pooled estimates.
Using only final endpoint reports produced pooled estimates that the authors judged not materially different from the primary analysis.
The pooled mean difference for HbA1c was -0.52 with a 95% CI from -0.6 to -0.45.

canonical_statement: Four included RCTs reported only short follow-up periods or interim results, limiting the available endpoint evidence.
The meta-analysis used only the 10 mg dapagliflozin dose for pooled comparisons because of dosage consistency, limiting dose-specific inference.
The limited number of RCTs could overestimate R-squared values in meta-regression.
Most included RCTs used last-observation-carried-forward imputation, and combining LOCF with exclusion of post-rescue data could overstate effects and underestimate standard errors and p values.
All included RCTs were sponsored by Bristol-Myers Squibb or AstraZeneca, which the authors identified as a potential source of bias.
Publication bias was detected for the body-weight outcome, reducing confidence in that pooled estimate.
The authors concluded that dapagliflozin added to conventional antidiabetic drugs improved glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes without significant body-weight gain.
The final conclusion states that dapagliflozin add-on therapy improved glycaemic control and reduced weight gain, especially when conventional drugs provided inadequate glycaemic control.
The authors planned to update the meta-analysis when further properly registered RCTs with less potential bias became available.
The authors reported University of Macau grant MYRG190-Y3-L3-ICMS11-LSW as funding for the work of YS, YZ, and SL.
The article reported no competing interests.
The data-sharing statement reported that no additional data were available.
